description: list_providers returns all enabled providers with live-discovered models
steps: Call list_providers MCP tool with no parameters
Verify response is valid JSON with 'providers' key
Verify only enabled providers (from settings.json) are included
Verify each provider has 'name', 'display_name', and 'models' array
Verify models are live-discovered (same as provider.get_models())

description: list_providers includes model metadata from ralph settings
steps: Configure ralph.providers.claude.model_metadata with cost_tier and best_for_tags
Call list_providers
Verify each model has 'id', 'cost_tier', 'best_for_tags', 'best_for_notes' fields
Verify metadata values match settings configuration
Verify models without metadata show null cost_tier and empty arrays

description: list_providers respects model allowlist/blocklist filtering
steps: Configure ralph.providers.claude.models_allowed = ['opus', 'sonnet']
Call list_providers
Verify claude provider's models contain only 'opus' and 'sonnet'
Verify 'haiku' is NOT in the models array

description: list_providers handles missing CLI gracefully
steps: Enable opencode provider but ensure opencode CLI is not installed
Call list_providers
Verify opencode provider appears with empty models array
Verify no crash - tool returns valid JSON

description: list_providers handles missing ralph settings section
steps: Remove the 'ralph' section from settings.json entirely
Call list_providers
Verify fallback to top-level providers with all live-discovered models
Verify models have null metadata (no cost_tier, empty tags)

description: invoke_provider sends prompt and returns CLI response for claude
steps: Call invoke_provider with provider='claude', model='haiku', prompt='Say hello in one word'
Verify response is a non-empty string containing the CLI's output
Verify no JSON wrapper on success - just the raw response text
Verify subprocess was spawned with claude -p --model haiku

description: invoke_provider sends prompt and returns CLI response for opencode
steps: Ensure opencode CLI is installed and configured
Call invoke_provider with provider='opencode', model from list_providers, prompt='Say hello'
Verify response is a non-empty string
Verify subprocess used opencode run --model <model>

description: invoke_provider pipes prompt via stdin (not CLI args)
steps: Call invoke_provider with a prompt containing special characters ($, ", newlines)
Verify prompt is passed via subprocess stdin pipe
Verify prompt does NOT appear in process command-line arguments
Verify response is received without shell injection issues

description: invoke_provider respects custom timeout parameter
steps: Call invoke_provider with timeout=5 and a prompt that would take longer
Verify tool returns error after approximately 5 seconds
Verify error message indicates timeout
Verify subprocess is killed (process tree terminated)

description: invoke_provider uses default timeout from settings when not specified
steps: Configure tools.providers.default_timeout = 60 in settings.json
Call invoke_provider without specifying timeout
Verify the subprocess timeout is 60 seconds (not the hardcoded 120)

description: invoke_provider returns error for unknown provider
steps: Call invoke_provider with provider='nonexistent'
Verify JSON error response with descriptive message
Verify available providers are listed in the error message

description: invoke_provider returns error for disabled provider
steps: Set providers.opencode.enabled = false in settings.json
Call invoke_provider with provider='opencode'
Verify JSON error response indicating provider is not enabled

description: invoke_provider returns error when CLI binary not found
steps: Enable a provider whose CLI is not installed
Call invoke_provider with that provider
Verify JSON error response indicating binary not found on PATH

description: invoke_provider returns error for unavailable model
steps: Call invoke_provider with provider='claude', model='nonexistent-model'
Verify JSON error response indicating model not available
Verify available models are listed in the error message

description: invoke_provider returns error when CLI process fails
steps: Call invoke_provider with a configuration that causes CLI to exit with non-zero code
Verify JSON error response including exit code
Verify stderr content is included in the error message

description: invoke_provider handles empty response from CLI
steps: Call invoke_provider with a prompt that produces no output
Verify empty string is returned (not an error)
Verify no JSON error wrapper

description: providers tool group follows tool_groups registration pattern
steps: Verify tool_groups/__init__.py has 'providers' in _TOOL_GROUPS dict
Verify tool_groups/providers_tools.py has register(mcp, settings) function
Verify server/config.py _TOOLS_DEFAULTS has 'providers' entry
Verify tools are registered when tools.providers.enabled = true
Verify tools are NOT registered when tools.providers.enabled = false

description: providers tool group registers without affecting teams or ralph tools
steps: Enable all three tool groups (teams, ralph, providers)
Start MCP server
Verify all 13 teams tools are registered
Verify all 5 ralph tools are registered
Verify both providers tools (list_providers, invoke_provider) are registered
Verify no naming conflicts between tool groups

description: Provider base class documents required vs optional methods
steps: Read Provider class docstring
Verify required methods are documented: get_models, get_chat_cmd, get_invocation
Verify optional methods with defaults are documented
Verify get_summarizer_command has fallback to get_chat_cmd

description: New provider can be added with minimal code
steps: Create a TestProvider subclass implementing only required methods
Add to _PROVIDER_REGISTRY
Add settings entry with enabled=true
Call list_providers
Verify new provider appears with its models
Call invoke_provider with new provider
Verify it works

description: invoke_provider works correctly on Windows
steps: Call invoke_provider on Windows
Verify CREATE_NO_WINDOW flag is set on subprocess
Verify .cmd/.bat wrappers are handled with cmd.exe /c prefix
Verify process tree is killed on timeout using taskkill /T /F

description: invoke_provider does not expose prompts in process arguments
steps: Call invoke_provider with a prompt containing sensitive data
Verify prompt is sent via stdin pipe, not as CLI argument
Verify prompt does not appear in process listing (tasklist / ps)

description: list_providers completes within 15 seconds
steps: Call list_providers with all providers enabled
Verify response received within 15 seconds
Verify each provider's model discovery has individual 10s timeout

description: Concurrent invoke_provider calls are independent
steps: Call invoke_provider twice concurrently with different providers
Verify both calls return independently
Verify no shared state corruption between calls
